content.title: U.S. Treasury Yields Are Stable Ahead of Fed Rate Decision
content.summary: Yields on U.S. Treasuries were stable in early trade as markets await the Federal Reserve's rate decision, most likely a 25-basis-point reduction.  "The probability is very high that the Fed will cut by 25 basis points tonight, and a 50-basis point cut cannot fully be ruled out," said SEB Research's FX and fixed income strategist Amanda Sundstrom in a note.  SEB expects the majority of FOMC to vote for 25-basis-point steps and that Fed Chair Jerome Powell will signal that there is scope for another cut at the next meeting, in October, the strategist said.

content.title: U.S. Treasuries Inch Up With Market Focus on Fed Rate Decision
content.summary: U.S. Treasury yields were marginally higher in early trade, with markets considering a 25-basis-point interest-rate cut by the Federal Reserve on Wednesday as a near certainty.  "The market is expecting a 25-basis point cut, which is generally the appropriate expectation," said Thornburg Investment Management's Lon Erickson in a note.  In his view, the market isn't ready for another 50-basis-point cut this year like the Fed did when the cutting process began a year ago.

content.title: U.S. 10-Year Treasury Yield Still at Higher End of Historic Range
content.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield remains at the higher end of its range since 2008, UBS strategists said in a note. This could allow scope for them to fall further, they said. Treasury yields have fallen in recent weeks on a growing conviction that Federal Reserve rate cuts are on their way.

content.title: U.S. Treasury Yields Move Higher, Fed Rate Cut Looms Next Week
content.summary: U.S. Treasury yields were rising in Asian trade, even as August CPI data published Thursday are unlikely to be a game changer in the Federal Reserve's policy outlook.  Following the data, "we left both our Fed outlook and our inflation forecasts unchanged," Pimco's Tiffany Wilding said in a note.  Accordingly, Pimco expects a 25-basis-point rate cut next week, "though 50 [basis points] will likely be discussed," the economist said.
